options.B: Feeding a patient who has a stroke
options.C: Inserting an indwelling urinary catheter
options.D: Taking routine vital signs in the morning

explanation: Inserting a urinary catheter enters a sterile body cavity, requiring surgical asepsis to prevent introducing bacteria into the bladder. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h2)

question: Which of the following is a direct health function of the PTA?

options.A: Stocking the school clinic with first aid materials
options.B: Performing surgical operations during emergencies
options.C: Prescribing antibiotics to sick students in class
options.D: Teaching all the mathematics lessons in school

explanation: Providing basic first aid supplies is a practical way the PTA helps manage minor health issues in school. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h2)

question: An Eastern Orthodox patient refuses lunch during a fast. What does this fast usually involve?

options.A: Eating only raw vegetables and avoiding all cooked grains
options.B: Complete abstention from all food and water from sunrise to sunset
options.C: Consuming only liquids and high-sugar supplements
options.D: Avoiding meat, dairy, and sometimes oil for designated days

explanation: During specific holy seasons, Eastern Orthodox fasting rules call for giving up animal products like meat and dairy. Knowing this helps us plan better meals for them!

question: What is the main goal of a clinically useful research problem?

options.A: Nursing care and patient health outcomes
options.B: The speed of administrative paperwork
options.C: The personal salary of the lead researcher
options.D: The architectural design of the hospital

explanation: At the end of the day, nursing research is all about making patient care safer and helping people recover better. That's why we do it!

question: What is a major logistical problem caused by uncoordinated disaster donations?

options.A: Relief workers spend all their time cooking donated food
options.B: Local markets experience a permanent surplus of luxury vehicles
options.C: Hospitals run out of storage space for monetary funds
options.D: Unwanted goods block transport routes while essential items get stuck

explanation: Sending random unrequested supplies clogs up ports and roads, delaying the delivery of life-saving medical gear. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h6)

question: Why is chronic kidney disease an important thing to note when taking a patient's blood history?

options.A: It triggers sudden and uncontrollable blood clotting
options.B: Damaged kidneys produce less erythropoietin, causing anaemia
options.C: It causes the liver to stop storing iron completely
options.D: Kidney failure immediately destroys all white blood cells

explanation: Healthy kidneys make erythropoietin, the hormone that tells the bone marrow to build red blood cells. When kidneys fail, that hormone drops, leading to anaemia.

question: A patient with newly diagnosed severe kidney disease needs help managing their protein and potassium intake. Which setting is best?

options.A: Individual counselling
options.B: General television health ads
options.C: Group dietary classes
options.D: A public community workshop

explanation: New, complex diagnoses need one-on-one attention to review lab values and build a safe, highly specific meal plan. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h2)

question: How do clinical software apps differ from system software?

options.A: Clinical apps perform specific job tasks like charting, while system software manages the computer itself.
options.B: System software is designed for patients, while clinical apps are for doctors only.
options.C: Clinical apps can only run without an operating system present.
options.D: Clinical apps are physical hardware parts, while system software is purely digital.

explanation: Clinical apps help you do your actual job (like charting vitals), while system software keeps the machine running behind the scenes.

question: What do we call the outward, social way a person shows their grief?

options.A: Depression
options.B: Denial
options.C: Mourning
options.D: Suffering

explanation: Mourning is simply the visible, cultural, and social actions people take to express their grief after a loss.

question: A wheelchair user visits the clinic complaining of unusual fatigue and constant thirst. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Investigate for potential systemic issues like diabetes
options.B: Refer the patient immediately to an orthotic specialist
options.C: Advise the patient to rest more and avoid further medical testing
options.D: Document that fatigue is a normal side effect of using a wheelchair

explanation: Never brush off new symptoms! Fatigue and thirst could mean something like diabetes, so they always deserve a proper check-up. You're thinking like a real nurse!

question: Why do cities usually record higher family planning use than rural villages?

options.A: Better access to equipped health facilities and higher literacy
options.B: Rural health workers refuse to distribute any commodities
options.C: Contraceptives are strictly forbidden by law in villages
options.D: Traditional beliefs are completely absent in big cities

explanation: Being close to clinics and having better access to health education makes it much easier for city residents to get and use family planning services.

question: What is the main goal of nursing care for a patient at the end of life?

options.A: Preventing all family visits
options.B: Promoting comfort and dignity
options.C: Curing the underlying disease
options.D: Speeding up the dying process

explanation: When a disease cannot be cured, nursing care shifts its focus to keeping the patient comfortable and maintaining their dignity. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T12#GNS321_U4_T12_h1)

question: Why does money collected from selling drugs in a DRF go right back into the fund instead of a general government account?

options.A: To ensure the money is immediately available to buy more drug stock
options.B: To pay off international government debts and loans
options.C: To cover the cost of unrelated building construction projects
options.D: To pay the personal salaries of the hospital management team

explanation: You got it! Keeping the money right where it is (ring-fencing it) ensures the pharmacy can restock quickly without waiting for government bureaucracy.

question: Which drug is commonly used first when a mother has postpartum hemorrhage from a soft uterus?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Paracetamol
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Furosemide

explanation: You got it! Oxytocin helps the uterine muscle contract strongly to stop heavy bleeding.

question: An elderly patient leaks small amounts of liquid stool daily. What should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Bacterial food poisoning
options.B: Severe ulcerative colitis flare
options.C: Normal recovery from constipation
options.D: Fecal impaction with overflow

explanation: Liquid stool often leaks around a hard, impacted blockage in the rectum, which can trick people into thinking it is diarrhea. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why do electronic blood pressure monitors need to be checked and calibrated regularly?

options.A: Internal sensors naturally drift and lose accuracy over time and with use
options.B: It's just a rule made by manufacturers to keep batteries from exploding
options.C: The internal software wipes its own memory clean every few weeks
options.D: Sensors magically improve their own accuracy without any human help

explanation: Just like weighing scales, electronic monitors can get a bit out of whack over time. Regular checks ensure our numbers stay trustworthy.

question: Which level of health care serves as the foundation or bedrock of the Nigerian health system?

options.A: Secondary health care
options.B: Tertiary health care
options.C: Primary health care
options.D: Private laboratory care

explanation: Primary health care is designed to be the first point of contact and the foundation of the entire health delivery system. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h2)

question: Which factor is most important for keeping a DRF cycle running successfully for years?

options.A: Strict financial discipline and accurate inventory monitoring
options.B: Relying exclusively on large, unpredictable international donations
options.C: Stopping all forms of health insurance participation in the hospital
options.D: Selling all essential medicines at extremely high commercial markups

explanation: You got it! Good bookkeeping, careful stock checks, and making sure money always finds its way back to inventory are the real keys to success.

question: Which of these is NOT a main job of the gonads?

options.A: Quickly fixing sudden drops in blood pressure
options.B: Supporting secondary sex traits like body hair
options.C: Helping with reproductive growth
options.D: Producing sex hormones like estrogen and testosterone

explanation: Spot on! Gonads focus on reproductive hormones. Blood pressure is managed by other organs like your kidneys and heart.

question: What kind of nursing assessment should you perform to uncover a patient's environmental risk factors?

options.A: A physical neurological reflex test only
options.B: A psychosocial assessment
options.C: An environmental soil analysis
options.D: A routine surgical checklist

explanation: A psychosocial assessment digs into the person's background, home life, relationships, and current life stressors.

question: What makes a histogram different from a regular bar chart?

options.A: The bars touch each other with no gaps
options.B: The bars are colored in bright shades
options.C: The chart includes a title at the top
options.D: The vertical axis measures percentages

explanation: Spot on! Bar charts have spaces between categories, but histograms touch because their numerical scale keeps right on going.

question: A mother is worried because her baby had a mild fever and swelling after their last shot. How should you respond?

options.A: Advise the mother never to bring the child back for any future immunizations
options.B: Report the child to public health authorities for failing a routine check
options.C: Explain that these mild reactions are normal signs of the immune system working
options.D: Immediately prescribe strong oral antibiotics to treat an expected infection

explanation: Spot on! A little soreness or low-grade fever just means the baby's immune system is busy building up its defenses.

question: Why is establishing cause and effect difficult in cross-sectional studies?

options.A: Statistical software cannot process percentages
options.B: Researchers always interview too few patients
options.C: Exposure and outcome are measured at the same time
options.D: Participants never answer questionnaires honestly

explanation: Since you check both the risk factor and the health issue at the exact same moment, it's tough to know which one happened first.

question: Which Nigerian government bodies coordinate national and state-level disaster management?

options.A: EFCC and ICPC
options.B: NEPA and PHCN
options.C: JAMB and WAEC
options.D: NEMA and SEMA

explanation: Good to know for your community health postings! NEMA handles things at the national level, while SEMA takes charge at the state level.

question: What is the main job of an enteric coating on a tablet?

options.A: To allow the nurse to crush the pill easily into food
options.B: To help the tablet dissolve much faster in the mouth
options.C: To make the pill taste sweet for children
options.D: To protect the stomach lining and prevent acid breakdown

explanation: Think of an enteric coating as a special shield! It helps the pill ignore harsh stomach acid so it can safely reach the small intestine before dissolving.

question: How does GNP treat profits earned by a foreign-owned company operating inside Nigeria?

options.A: They are added directly to Nigeria's GNP
options.B: They are converted into government bonds
options.C: They are doubled in Nigeria's GNP
options.D: They are excluded from Nigeria's GNP

explanation: Remember, GNP only counts output generated by citizens and permanent residents, so foreign-owned production inside the country is left out.

question: What is a major downside of relying only on text-heavy pamphlets in a rural community?

options.A: They take too long to read during a surgical procedure.
options.B: They are too expensive for the federal government to print.
options.C: They are ineffective for community members with low literacy levels.
options.D: They encourage people to ignore traditional folk songs.

explanation: Spot on! If people cannot read easily, text-heavy flyers won't help. That's why pictures, radio, and drama are often much better choices.

question: How do broken elevators and inaccessible buildings directly affect a disabled person's mental health?

options.A: They automatically cure chronic depression by forcing daily exercise
options.B: They improve social bonds by encouraging neighbors to carry people
options.C: They have no impact on emotions, only on physical fitness
options.D: They lead to physical exclusion, which triggers deep loneliness and isolation

explanation: That's right. When buildings aren't accessible, individuals get trapped at home, cutting off their social life and leading to heavy isolation.

question: If you are talking to local village elders about building a new maternity clinic, how should you pitch it?

options.A: Discuss advanced surgical techniques used in teaching hospitals
options.B: Focus on family health, community safety, and local traditions
options.C: Present complex statistical models on maternal mortality ratios
options.D: Emphasize strict government legal codes and budget allocations

explanation: You're doing great! Village elders want to hear about real, practical things that protect and respect their families and community traditions.

question: A patient is admitted with sudden, severe confusion and mood swings. What must the nurse consider first based on biological etiology?

options.A: Whether an underlying physical illness or hormone imbalance is causing the symptoms
options.B: How long the patient has been using herbal sleeping mixtures
options.C: Which family member caused the patient to feel stressed recently
options.D: If the patient experienced a difficult childhood in the village

explanation: Medical issues like thyroid problems or infections can cause psychiatric symptoms, so biological causes must be investigated during assessment. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h2)

question: How does quality improvement differ from traditional quality assurance?

options.A: Quality improvement ignores patient outcomes to focus entirely on financial savings.
options.B: Quality assurance is only used in surgical units, while quality improvement is used everywhere.
options.C: Quality improvement looks at fixing underlying processes, while quality assurance often focuses on finding faults after they happen.
options.D: Quality assurance focuses on ongoing system redesign, while quality improvement looks for individual faults.

explanation: Great job thinking this through! Old-school quality assurance usually looks backward to find someone to blame, but quality improvement looks forward to fix the process so it works smoothly.

question: Why must a hospital's internal policy always respect national nursing council regulations?

options.A: National councils pay for the printing of hospital rulebooks
options.B: It makes the hospital paperwork look neat and organized
options.C: Lower-level policies can never contradict higher regulatory frameworks
options.D: It allows nurses to ignore doctors' written prescriptions

explanation: In healthcare law, local rules must always align with and support higher national laws and professional board regulations.

question: You notice raw chicken breasts stored directly above fresh lettuce in the fridge. What is the immediate danger?

options.A: Rapid spoilage of the chicken caused by the nearby lettuce
options.B: Loss of nutritional value in the lettuce due to cold burn
options.C: Cross-contamination from raw meat juices dripping onto the lettuce
options.D: Chemical contamination from refrigerator coolant

explanation: Always store raw meat on the lowest shelf! This simple habit stops raw juices from dripping onto ready-to-eat foods below.

question: What does client-centered contraceptive counseling prioritize above all else?

options.A: The personal reproductive goals and choices of the client
options.B: The hospital policy on family planning targets
options.C: The nurse's personal preference for birth control methods
options.D: The fastest and cheapest method available in the clinic

explanation: Client-centered care centers entirely on the individual's needs, preferences, and life circumstances rather than outside pressures. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h2)

question: How do unit managers usually help with hospital budgeting?

options.A: By setting the salaries for all doctors in the country
options.B: By deciding which private bank holds hospital funds
options.C: By predicting future equipment and supply needs for their ward
options.D: By collecting taxes from patients upon discharge

explanation: Great thinking! Managers know their wards best, so they help the finance team by forecasting what materials and tools their department will need.

question: Which of these is a dangerous trap nurses should avoid when assessing patient pain?

options.A: Asking about the location of the discomfort
options.B: Believing that self-report is always the best method
options.C: Assuming a sleeping patient is completely free of pain
options.D: Using a 0-10 scale for adults with normal cognition

explanation: Never assume sleep means zero pain! Exhaustion can cause patients to drift off even when they are hurting badly.

question: Which core principle of community health nursing is all about fairness and helping vulnerable groups first?

options.A: Rigid institutional control
options.B: Medical dominance
options.C: Hospital centralization
options.D: Equity in care

explanation: Well done! Equity means making sure resources go where they are needed most so everyone has a fair chance at good health.

question: In research, what does the 'validity' of a questionnaire mean?

options.A: Whether the tool can be completed in under ten minutes
options.B: Whether the tool measures what it is intended to measure
options.C: Whether the tool was printed on approved institutional paper
options.D: Whether the tool gives the exact same scores on repeat testing

explanation: Validity checks if your questions are truly capturing the specific concept or variable you set out to study. You're building solid clinical research skills!

question: Why should the head of a patient's bed be kept elevated while they are on a mechanical ventilator?

options.A: To reduce the risk of gastric contents entering the lungs
options.B: To increase the speed of the ventilator motor
options.C: To help the nurse chart more comfortably
options.D: To make it easier for visitors to see the patient's face

explanation: Gravity is on our side when the bed is raised. It keeps stomach acid and food where they belong—down in the stomach!

question: What is the main danger of burning medical waste in open drums instead of using proper high-temperature incinerators?

options.A: It releases toxic air pollutants like dioxins into the local atmosphere
options.B: It creates underground tremors that weaken nearby hospital foundations
options.C: It automatically purifies all the plastic materials into harmless ash
options.D: It causes the surrounding groundwater to freeze solid instantly

explanation: Correct! Low-temperature open burning doesn't break down complex chemicals safely; instead, it pumps dangerous pollutants and toxins right into the air we breathe.

question: Standard precautions apply to which of these body fluids in the ward?

options.A: Sweat from a patient exercising in physical therapy
options.B: Clean tap water used for bed baths
options.C: Saliva and wound drainage from a post-operative client
options.D: Tears collected after an eye examination

explanation: Spot on! Standard precautions cover all body fluids—except sweat. Saliva and wound drainage can carry germs, so we always protect ourselves. You are thinking like a real nurse!

question: What is the main purpose of a Service-Level Agreement (SLA) in healthcare outsourcing?

options.A: To set the salary scales for all nurses working in the outsourced department
options.B: To clearly define expected performance standards and quality metrics for the vendor
options.C: To legally transfer full ownership of the hospital building to the contractor
options.D: To determine how much profit the private company can distribute to shareholders

explanation: An SLA is like a clear contract or rulebook that sets the expected standards of work so everyone knows what good service looks like.

question: A nurse finds a toddler in an oxygen tent with damp clothes and cool skin. What should you do first?

options.A: Change the damp clothing and check the tent cooling settings
options.B: Administer an antipyretic medication for potential fever
options.C: Increase the oxygen flow rate on the wall flowmeter
options.D: Remove the child from the tent and place a nasal cannula

explanation: Moisture inside the tent can get clothes wet, which makes the child cold fast. Dressing them in dry clothes keeps them cozy and safe!

question: What does 'Total Fertility Rate' (TFR) actually measure?

options.A: The percentage of women using modern family planning methods
options.B: The average number of children a woman has during her reproductive years
options.C: The average age of mothers when giving birth to their first child
options.D: The total number of children born in a single hospital annually

explanation: Exactly! TFR estimates the average number of children a woman is expected to have throughout her childbearing years.

question: A patient scheduled for MVA is visibly shaking and expresses fear of severe pain. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Sit close, explain the steps calmly, and offer emotional reassurance
options.B: Cancel the procedure immediately and reschedule for another day
options.C: Tell her that pain is minor and she should try to stay strong
options.D: Administer a strong general anesthetic drug without a doctor's order

explanation: Anxious patients benefit greatly from calm explanations, validation of their feelings, and reassurance, which helps reduce physical tension and perceived pain. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h4)

question: Your clinical instructor praises you in front of the ward for a clean hand hygiene routine. What concept is this?

options.A: Extinction protocol
options.B: Negative reinforcement
options.C: Positive reinforcement
options.D: Constructivist scaffolding

explanation: Well done! Giving praise adds a feel-good reward right after a great action, making you much more likely to repeat it next time.

question: What is the primary focus of modern occupational health nursing?

options.A: Promoting and protecting worker well-being
options.B: Providing long-term hospital bedside care
options.C: Designing factory machinery and tools
options.D: Managing corporate financial portfolios

explanation: Occupational health nursing centers on safeguarding the health, safety, and overall well-being of employees across various work environments. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h1)

question: A sunken fontanelle is most commonly a classic sign of what condition?

options.A: Hydrocephalus
options.B: Skull fracture
options.C: Meningitis
options.D: Dehydration

explanation: Correct! When a baby loses body fluids from illness or poor feeding, fluid levels drop and the soft spot dips inward.

question: Which statement best describes how research studies treat hypotheses?

options.A: The hypothesis is always proven wrong in clinical trials
options.B: Data either supports the hypothesis or fails to support it
options.C: A successful study proves the hypothesis is an absolute law
options.D: Hypotheses are proven true without needing statistical tests

explanation: Science is a journey! We don't claim absolute truth from one study; our data simply supports our guess or tells us to look closer.

question: A patient on a new psychiatric drug is refusing to eat due to severe dry mouth. Who should the nurse consult first?

options.A: The medical records coding and billing department
options.B: The registered dietitian and the prescribing psychiatrist
options.C: The hospital maintenance and facility management team
options.D: The security personnel assigned to the psychiatric unit

explanation: You got it! A dietitian can help modify food textures for dry mouth, while the psychiatrist can review the medication dosage.

question: Why is teaching workers about toxic gases important in factories and industrial sites?

options.A: It helps workers recognize hidden breathing hazards and use safety gear
options.B: It eliminates the need for any medical staff on site
options.C: It reduces the cost of electricity in factories
options.D: It guarantees that machinery will never break down

explanation: Many toxic gases are invisible. Educating workers helps them spot dangers early and protect themselves with proper ventilation and masks.

question: When does heavy milk production (known as Lactogenesis II) typically kick in after childbirth?

options.A: 48 to 72 hours postpartum
options.B: Immediately upon delivery of the baby
options.C: Only after weaning the infant
options.D: Two weeks after childbirth

explanation: It usually takes about 2 to 3 days after delivery for the hormones to shift and the 'milk to come in' in large amounts.

question: You notice two drugs with very similar names and packaging sitting right next to each other, leading to a close call. What should you do?

options.A: Ignore the incident since no actual patient was harmed this time
options.B: Write a formal warning letter to the pharmacist who stocked the shelf
options.C: Tell all nurses in the unit to read medication labels much slower
options.D: Relocate one medication to a different shelf and report the labeling issue

explanation: Brilliant! Changing where the drugs are stored fixes the environmental hazard right away and stops future mix-ups.

question: Which of these is a classic example of an obstetric risk factor?

options.A: Chronic kidney disease
options.B: A history of recurrent miscarriages
options.C: Smoking cigarettes daily
options.D: Young maternal age under seventeen

explanation: Obstetric factors are linked right to a woman's past pregnancies and birth history, like previous miscarriages or early deliveries.

question: Why do doctors often ask for multiple stool samples when testing for intestinal parasites?

options.A: Laboratories require a large bulk sample for chemical mixing
options.B: Single samples automatically get lost during transport
options.C: Parasites are not always shed continuously in every stool
options.D: Infection levels change every single hour of the day

explanation: That's right! Because the parasite isn't passed out in every single bowel movement, checking samples over a few days boosts your chances of catching it.

question: When do Lassa fever outbreaks usually peak in Nigeria?

options.A: November to May
options.B: Throughout the entire year equally
options.C: September to October
options.D: June to August

explanation: You'll see more cases during the dry season. Bush burning and farming drive rodents closer to human homes looking for food and shelter.

question: What happens to the actual length of thick and thin filaments when a muscle contracts?

options.A: They stretch out to make the sarcomere longer
options.B: They shorten significantly as the muscle contracts
options.C: They dissolve completely and reform later
options.D: They stay the same length while sliding past each other

explanation: A common trick question! The filaments themselves don't shrink or stretch; they just slide past each other like two combs interlocking. Smooth moves! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h5)

question: Which Nigerian agency is in charge of enforcing environmental and waste laws?

options.A: Nigerian Football Federation
options.B: NESREA
options.C: National Youth Service Corps
options.D: Federal Road Safety Corps

explanation: Spot on! NESREA (National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency) sets and enforces laws to protect Nigeria's environment.

question: How should a nurse correct a writing error in a paper health record?

options.A: Tear out the entire page of the notebook and start the report over
options.B: Draw a single line through the error, write 'mistaken entry', sign, and date it
options.C: Scratch out the wrong words heavily with a pen until no one can read them
options.D: Use correction fluid (tipp-ex) to completely cover the mistake until invisible

explanation: Using a single line preserves readability of the original error, preventing suspicions of tampering or hidden alterations. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h8)

question: How does fee-for-service differ fundamentally from capitation?

options.A: Providers are paid based on each specific test or treatment performed
options.B: Patients pay the doctor directly with farm produce
options.C: The hospital receives the exact same amount every month forever
options.D: No money changes hands until the end of the calendar year

explanation: Under fee-for-service, payment is tied directly to the volume of services rendered rather than a fixed advance sum per patient. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h5)

question: If a home care family is struggling financially and needs help finding community resources, who is the best professional to call?

options.A: Registered Dietitian
options.B: Wound Care Specialist
options.C: Medical Social Worker
options.D: Physical Therapist

explanation: Medical social workers are pros at navigating financial aid, government packages, and community support programs to help struggling families.

question: What happens to the endometrium (lining of the uterus) when pregnancy does not happen?

options.A: It transforms into permanent scar tissue inside the cavity
options.B: It hardens into a protective barrier for the cervix
options.C: It travels up the fallopian tubes to dissolve in the ovary
options.D: It sheds and leaves the body as menstrual flow

explanation: Spot on! When there's no fertilized egg to welcome, hormone levels drop and this lining sheds during your period.

question: How did the pre-Alma-Ata medical model contribute to severe health disparities?

options.A: By placing too much emphasis on handwashing and clean water over medicine
options.B: By locking resources and trained staff in cities while rural populations were left neglected
options.C: By forcing doctors to travel constantly to remote villages instead of staying in labs
options.D: By making prescription drugs too cheap for pharmaceutical companies to survive

explanation: Concentrating medical resources in urban centers meant poor and rural populations had little to no access to basic healthcare. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is the biggest advantage of giving a client card directly to the patient to keep?

options.A: It saves the clinic money on buying storage cabinets
options.B: It prevents the clinic from ever writing anything down
options.C: It forces the patient to become a trained community health worker
options.D: The patient carries their health history with them to any new facility

explanation: Exactly right! Portable client cards ensure a patient's immunization and health history travels with them safely, even if they move away.

question: What is the true spirit of 'supportive supervision' in primary healthcare?

options.A: Conducting annual written examinations without site visits
options.B: Visiting clinics strictly to penalize workers for minor errors
options.C: Outsourcing all facility management to private auditing firms
options.D: Mentoring and working alongside staff to solve problems

explanation: Supportive supervisors are like encouraging coaches! They visit to guide, teach, and help staff solve daily challenges, not just to look for mistakes.

question: How does proper financial control directly help patient care?

options.A: It completely removes the need for doctors to write prescriptions
options.B: It allows nurses to spend less time documenting patient symptoms
options.C: It guarantees that patients never have to wait in the emergency room
options.D: It ensures necessary equipment and medications are available when needed

explanation: When money is managed well, your ward will steadily have the tools, drugs, and supplies required to treat patients safely.

question: Why does a high patient-to-nurse ratio make nursing audits difficult?

options.A: Nurses are too overwhelmed with direct patient care to conduct or participate in audits
options.B: Paper case notes will disappear from the wards every single night
options.C: Patients will refuse to let doctors check their vital signs
options.D: Hospitals will automatically close down all nursing schools

explanation: Spot on! When nurses are stretched thin caring for too many patients at once, finding extra time for chart reviews and quality improvement is tough.

question: What happens in a healthcare facility that loves to punish and blame staff?

options.A: Nurses become more eager to report system failures
options.B: Medical errors are completely eliminated from the wards
options.C: Interprofessional communication improves significantly
options.D: Staff hide their mistakes and near-misses out of fear

explanation: Spot on! A heavy blame culture drives mistakes underground. When staff are terrified of punishment, nobody speaks up so the team can learn from it.

question: Which of these does NOT cause an error when using an infrared thermometer?

options.A: Bringing the device straight from a cold room into a warm ward
options.B: Using a brand new disposable probe cover
options.C: Heavy sweat on the patient's forehead
options.D: Accumulated earwax in the ear canal

explanation: A clean probe cover is what you *want* to use! It keeps things hygienic and won't mess up your reading.

question: Why might a nurse choose the FOUR Score instead of the Glasgow Coma Scale for a patient who has a breathing tube?

options.A: The FOUR Score completely eliminates the need for physical assessments.
options.B: The FOUR Score uses numbers ranging from 1 to 100 for easier math.
options.C: The FOUR Score assesses brainstem reflexes and respiration, which an intubated patient cannot voice.
options.D: The FOUR Score takes less than five seconds to complete in any setting.

explanation: Because a breathing tube stops a patient from talking, the GCS verbal score becomes useless. The FOUR Score is great because it checks brainstem reflexes and breathing instead!

question: What happens when 'noise' or interference enters the communication process?

options.A: It speeds up how fast the sender talks to the receiver
options.B: It disrupts the message and can lead to misunderstandings
options.C: It changes the communication channel into a written format
options.D: It automatically guarantees the client will follow instructions

explanation: Noise represents any barrier or distraction that gets in the way of clear message transmission between sender and receiver. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h2)

question: A client comes back complaining of mild spotting a month after getting an implant. How should you respond?

options.A: Tell her she has a serious pelvic infection
options.B: Take out the implant immediately and offer nothing else
options.C: Reassure her that this is a normal and common side effect
options.D: Tell her to stop drinking water for two days

explanation: Spot on! Pre-counseling helps clients stay calm. Reassuring them that spotting is normal builds great trust and keeps them comfortable.

question: Which phase of disaster monitoring involves watching weather patterns and community vulnerabilities before an event hits?

options.A: Post-disaster phase
options.B: Recovery-only phase
options.C: Pre-disaster phase
options.D: Trans-disaster phase

explanation: The pre-disaster phase focuses on preparation, tracking risks, and looking at weather or health data before a crisis occurs. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h2)

question: A relative suddenly gets angry and pulls away during a visit. How should you, as a nurse, view this behavior?

options.A: As a sign that the relative wishes to abandon the patient
options.B: As proof that the relative does not care about the patient
options.C: As a normal reaction during the process of anticipatory grief
options.D: As a personal insult directed at the nursing staff

explanation: Don't take it personally! Anger and withdrawal are just natural ways people react when they are struggling to accept an impending, painful loss.

question: Which action best demonstrates the nurse's role in interprofessional drug information exchange?

options.A: Consulting with the hospital pharmacist to clarify an ambiguous drug dosage order
options.B: Writing the discharge prescription without consulting the medical team
options.C: Changing a patient's medication dose independently when side effects appear
options.D: Deciding which new drugs the hospital pharmacy committee should purchase

explanation: Working closely with pharmacists ensures safe medication practices through collaborative communication. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T3#GNS215_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why is knowing the chain of infection so helpful for nurses?

options.A: It shows the exact cost of treating a hospital-acquired infection
options.B: It guides how to stop germs from spreading by breaking a link
options.C: It proves which specific antibiotic will cure the patient
options.D: It helps predict how long a patient will stay in the hospital

explanation: Spot on! When nurses understand how infections travel, we can step in and break any part of the chain to keep our patients safe.

question: A child is forced to weave in a dark room for twelve hours daily. What category of trafficking is this?

options.A: Commercial sex trade
options.B: Illegal adoption
options.C: Domestic servitude
options.D: Forced child labor

explanation: Working long hours in production or hazardous trades falls under forced child labor rather than house chores.

question: What is the classic description of the walking pattern often seen in late pregnancy?

options.A: A fast shuffling stride
options.B: An unsteady staggering gait
options.C: A stiff-legged military march
options.D: A wide-based waddling gait

explanation: Pregnant women naturally widen their stance and swing their hips slightly more to maintain balance over relaxed joints and a heavy abdomen. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h5)

question: What responsibility do nurses hold regarding data integrity in the electronic health record?

options.A: Ensuring accurate and timely data entry to protect patient safety
options.B: Writing the underlying computer code for the hospital software
options.C: Repairing broken hardware terminals in patient rooms
options.D: Setting up new user accounts for incoming hospital doctors

explanation: Nurses must enter correct information carefully because mistakes in the chart can directly harm patient care. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why is collaboration between schools and local primary health centers important?

options.A: It creates a smooth referral pathway for immunization and clinical care
options.B: It allows the school to take over full control of the clinic
options.C: It stops community members from seeking traditional medicine
options.D: It ensures that students never have to visit a hospital again

explanation: Local health centers provide backup support for vaccination drives, medical referrals, and complex treatments beyond school capacity. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h7)

question: Why is Vitamin K so effective at reversing the effects of warfarin?

options.A: It speeds up kidney filtration so warfarin leaves in the urine
options.B: It thickens the liquid plasma to stop bleeding instantly
options.C: It destroys the warfarin molecules floating in the blood
options.D: It bypasses the enzyme block to help the liver resume making clotting factors

explanation: Since warfarin blocks Vitamin K, giving extra Vitamin K gives the liver the exact ingredients it needs to get back to making clotting factors.

question: How does losing access to school affect a young bride's future?

options.A: It makes her physically unable to speak clearly to healthcare workers
options.B: It limits her ability to earn money and understand basic health information
options.C: It forces her to move permanently to a foreign country
options.D: It guarantees she will develop severe bone disorders in old age

explanation: Well reasoned! Without education, she misses out on financial independence and health awareness, keeping her trapped in vulnerability.

question: What is the main difference between GDP and GNP?

options.A: GDP is calculated monthly while GNP is calculated every decade
options.B: GDP includes inflation while GNP excludes all taxes
options.C: GDP measures health services while GNP measures manufactured goods
options.D: GDP uses geographic location while GNP uses ownership and citizenship

explanation: The core distinction is simple: GDP cares about where production happens, while GNP cares about who owns the production.

question: What is usually the very first formal step when investigating a suspected disease outbreak?

options.A: Burn all personal belongings of infected residents
options.B: Verify the clinical diagnosis through laboratory testing
options.C: Construct a brand new tertiary care hospital
options.D: Close all international borders immediately

explanation: Before jumping to conclusions or panicking, public health teams must first confirm through lab tests that the suspected germ is actually there.

question: Why are formal nursing homes slowly becoming more common in modern Nigeria?

options.A: Elderly individuals prefer living away from relatives
options.B: Traditional family values have completely disappeared
options.C: Urban migration and changing economic structures
options.D: A government ban on caring for elders at home

explanation: Spot on! As younger family members move to busy cities for work and economic pressures rise, traditional home care setups have become harder to maintain.

question: What is the main job of psychological defense mechanisms?

options.A: To permanently cure chronic depression
options.B: To improve physical muscle strength under stress
options.C: To shield the mind from sudden emotional pain and anxiety
options.D: To increase conscious awareness of personal faults

explanation: Think of defense mechanisms as a mental shock absorber. They protect us unconsciously when stress or bad news feels too heavy to process all at once.

question: What is the main purpose of asset mapping in a community assessment?

options.A: To count how many people have severe mental illnesses
options.B: To find out how much money the local government has stolen
options.C: To locate abandoned buildings for quarantine centers
options.D: To identify existing local strengths and support systems

explanation: Asset mapping focuses on discovering what positive resources, skills, and groups already exist within the community to help solve problems. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h4)

question: Why does too much heat around the testes negatively affect a man's fertility?

options.A: It prevents the proper production and movement of sperm
options.B: It destroys the testosterone receptors in the liver
options.C: It stops the prostate gland from making seminal fluid
options.D: It causes an immediate blockage of the urethra

explanation: Correct! Sperm love a cool environment. Too much heat slows them down and stops them from forming properly. Another one in the bag!

question: Why do hospital disaster plans include steps for safely discharging stable patients?

options.A: To free up critical bed space and medical resources for incoming disaster casualties
options.B: To comply with international travel regulations for foreign medical volunteers
options.C: To punish patients who have overstayed their expected recovery duration
options.D: To reduce the hospital's monthly utility bills during a crisis event

explanation: When an emergency brings in dozens of critically injured people, sending home stable patients creates the vital bed space needed to save lives.

question: Which of the following is NOT a reason why nurses must follow strict infection control during an epidemic?

options.A: To prevent the nurse from contracting the infectious agent
options.B: To protect other vulnerable patients admitted to the ward
options.C: To stop the hospital environment from spreading the disease
options.D: To guarantee that patients pay their hospital bills on time

explanation: Brilliant! Infection control is entirely about safety and stopping the spread of germs, and has nothing to do with hospital bills or payments.

question: How do poor food supply systems directly impact clinical nursing practice?

options.A: By forcing nurses to work directly as agricultural extension officers
options.B: By completely eliminating the need for hospital admission records
options.C: By reducing the total number of patients seeking emergency care
options.D: By increasing cases of malnutrition and diet-related illnesses

explanation: Inadequate food systems lead directly to health conditions like malnutrition and chronic diseases that nurses treat in clinical settings. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h1)

question: What is the main difference between recruitment and selection?

options.A: Recruitment fires poor workers, while selection hires new replacements
options.B: Recruitment tests practical skills, while selection writes the job description
options.C: Recruitment is done only internally, while selection is done only externally
options.D: Recruitment attracts applicants, while selection chooses the best candidate

explanation: Easy way to remember: recruitment casts a wide net to get people to apply, while selection is the screening process where you pick the best person for the job.

question: What does self-medication mean in everyday terms?

options.A: Participating in a clinical drug trial supervised by researchers
options.B: Using medicines to treat self-recognized symptoms without a prescription
options.C: Receiving intravenous medications exclusively inside a hospital ward
options.D: Taking drugs strictly prescribed and monitored by a licensed physician

explanation: Self-medication simply means buying or taking drugs on your own to treat symptoms without getting a doctor's go-ahead first. You've got this!

question: Which clinical finding shows up early in a measles infection?

options.A: Yellow discoloration of the eye sclera
options.B: Painful spasms of the jaw muscles
options.C: Koplik spots inside the oral cavity
options.D: A thick grey membrane in the throat

explanation: Spot on! Koplik spots look like tiny grains of salt on a red background inside the cheeks, and they are a dead giveaway for early measles.

question: What is the defining feature of a Cost-Benefit Analysis in healthcare?

options.A: Outcomes are measured strictly in natural clinical units like blood pressure
options.B: Both costs and health outcomes are measured in monetary terms
options.C: It completely ignores financial expenses to focus on patient emotions
options.D: It is only used when two treatments produce identical results

explanation: In a Cost-Benefit Analysis, even the health outcomes are converted into money (like naira). This lets you directly compare cash spent to cash saved or earned.

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to prevent software-related mistakes on the ward?

options.A: Disabling all confirmation prompts to make data entry go faster
options.B: Using smart defaults that fill in safe, common choices
options.C: Limiting pop-up warnings only to true clinical hazards
options.D: Designing clear visual layouts with readable fonts

explanation: You nailed it! Confirmation prompts act as a vital safety net. Removing them just to type faster invites accidental medication or charting errors.

question: Which macronutrient has the most direct and immediate impact on blood glucose levels?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Proteins
options.C: Fats
options.D: Water

explanation: Carbohydrates break down rapidly into glucose during digestion, causing a direct rise in blood sugar. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h2)

question: A staff nurse sets a personal goal to use the SBAR communication tool during every patient handover this week. What level of objective is this?

options.A: Mission statement apex objective
options.B: Strategic executive objective
options.C: Long-term fiscal objective
options.D: Individual and operational objective

explanation: Daily practice goals set for a specific staff member fall at the base of the objective hierarchy. [learn more](GST321_U2_T3#GST321_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why is proper sampling important when conducting a descriptive survey in a hospital?

options.A: It guarantees that every single patient in the country will be cured
options.B: It removes the need to analyze numerical data at the end
options.C: It stops patients from answering survey questions incorrectly
options.D: It ensures the selected group accurately reflects the entire patient population

explanation: Good sampling means the few people you study are a true mini-version of the whole group, making your findings reliable. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h5)

question: Why are nurses considered the frontline of patient safety in a hospital?

options.A: Because they perform all the laboratory and pharmacy tests
options.B: Because they write all the medical and surgical treatment policies
options.C: Because they hold the legal responsibility for hospital finances
options.D: Because they spend the most continuous time at the patient's bedside

explanation: Because nurses are constantly with patients, they are in the best position to spot early signs of trouble and catch errors. [learn more](GST319_U4_T6#GST319_U4_T6_h6)

question: Which of these is a core pillar of the National Drug Policy?

options.A: Mandatory retirement age for pharmacists
options.B: Quality, safety, and efficacy of medicines
options.C: Privatization of all public teaching hospitals
options.D: Elimination of nursing schools in rural areas

explanation: Spot on! Making sure drugs are safe, work properly (efficacy), and are top quality is the heart of any good drug policy.

question: What is the core idea behind cultural competence in nursing?

options.A: Refusing to treat patients who consult traditional healers
options.B: Speaking only English during all patient health education sessions
options.C: Forcing patients to abandon their native beliefs in favor of modern science
options.D: Respecting patient traditions while promoting safe and effective health practices

explanation: Exactly! Cultural competence means honoring where our patients come from and blending their values with safe, evidence-based nursing care.

question: How does surveillance help us check if a vaccination campaign worked?

options.A: By calculating the exact salary of the nurses giving the shots
options.B: By showing whether disease rates drop after the vaccines are given
options.C: By tracking how many nurses attended the training workshop
options.D: By testing the chemical composition of vaccine vials

explanation: By keeping track of sickness rates over time, public health teams can easily tell if giving out those vaccines actually stopped the disease.

question: What special food product is lifesaver for treating severe malnutrition in emergencies?

options.A: High-sodium carbonated soft drinks
options.B: Ready-to-use therapeutic foods (RUTF)
options.C: Frozen commercial beef burgers
options.D: Standard multi-vitamin tablet bottles

explanation: RUTFs (like nutrient-packed peanut pastes) don't need water or refrigeration, making them perfect for quickly nursing severely malnourished children back to health.

question: What is the main goal when doing rehabilitation care for older adults?

options.A: Accelerating the normal aging process in the body
options.B: Curing all chronic illnesses present in the patient
options.C: Maximizing the patient's independence and function
options.D: Providing permanent custodial nursing home placement

explanation: You're doing great! Gerontological rehab is all about helping older adults do as much as they can for themselves, rather than just chasing a cure for old age. Keep it up!

question: A researcher spots a few strange blood pressure numbers that look like typos in the database. What is the best first step?

options.A: Ignore the mistakes and run the statistical analysis anyway
options.B: Change the numbers randomly to fit the average reading
options.C: Check the original paper records to verify the correct entry
options.D: Delete all the patient records so they do not ruin the study

explanation: Data cleaning means checking suspicious entries against original source documents rather than guessing or deleting data carelessly.

question: Why is classifying emergencies especially vital when many patients arrive at once?

options.A: It allows nurses to discharge everyone without a full examination
options.B: It ensures limited resources go to the most critical patients
options.C: It ensures all patients are treated in the exact order of arrival
options.D: It completely stops the need for doctors in the emergency room

explanation: When many people need help at the same time, sorting them makes sure that staff and equipment are not wasted on minor issues before severe ones are handled. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T1#GNS315_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is it so important to involve different specialists (like social workers) when a client has complex psychosocial needs?

options.A: It ensures specialized, long-term support beyond general nursing scope
options.B: It allows the nurse to stop visiting the client's home entirely
options.C: It guarantees that the client's physical illness will be cured
options.D: It replaces the need for family involvement in client care

explanation: Nurses wear many hats, but emotional and financial tangles often need dedicated experts. Bringing in social workers and counselors ensures the client gets the deep-dive help they deserve.

question: Why is protecting health information harder in a home setting than in a hospital?

options.A: Patients demand that their records be posted on the front door
options.B: Family members, visitors, and housemates are frequently present in the care area
options.C: Home health nurses are not bound by legal privacy rules
options.D: Hospitals do not have strict privacy laws

explanation: Spot on! Homes are busy places with people walking in and out, making it easy for others to accidentally overhear health matters or see your notes.

question: What does holistic nursing care require nurses to address alongside physical needs?

options.A: Spiritual and emotional needs
options.B: Financial planning records
options.C: Dietary supplement costs
options.D: Legal guardianship papers

explanation: Holistic nursing looks at the entire person, which includes physical, emotional, and spiritual dimensions of health. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T13#GNS225_U5_T13_h1)

question: What is the big superpower of adaptive immunity compared to innate immunity?

options.A: It requires no cellular involvement to neutralize foreign agents
options.B: It responds instantly within seconds of the very first infection
options.C: It relies solely on physical barriers like the skin and mucous
options.D: It develops long-term immunological memory for specific pathogens

explanation: Adaptive immunity keeps a memory of past infections. That way, if the same germ attacks again, your body mounts a much stronger and faster defense!

question: You are prepping surgical forceps that will go straight into a patient's sterile belly during surgery. What must you do to this equipment?

options.A: Low-level surface wiping
options.B: High-level disinfection
options.C: Sterilization
options.D: Mechanical washing only

explanation: Spot on! Anything entering sterile body tissues is a critical item and absolutely must be sterilized to prevent serious patient infections.

question: What is a major infrastructure challenge facing EHR implementation in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Unstable power supply and unreliable internet connectivity
options.B: Complete refusal of patients to allow digital data collection
options.C: Too many software options created by local nursing students
options.D: An overabundance of computer hardware in rural clinics

explanation: Consistent electricity and internet access are essential for digital health records, making power outages a major operational barrier. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h5)

question: As a nurse, what is an important rule to remember when checking in on a traumatized patient?

options.A: Rely solely on written questionnaires handed out at the triage desk
options.B: Ignore non-verbal cues and focus entirely on laboratory values
options.C: Insist that the patient describe every frightening moment in detail
options.D: Avoid forcing the patient to recount traumatic details immediately

explanation: Spot on! Never pressure a survivor to retell a scary story before they are ready. Pushing too hard can actually re-traumatize them. Let them take their time. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T3#GNS314_U6_T3_h4)

question: A nurse manager wants a new pressure sore prevention check to stick. What is the most effective strategy?

options.A: Keep the new check a secret until the end of the year evaluation
options.B: Add the check directly into the routine vital sign documentation round
options.C: Require nurses to write a separate essay report every single morning
options.D: Punish any nurse who forgets to mention the project in weekly meetings

explanation: Aligning new tasks with existing routines prevents them from feeling like burdensome extra chores. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h2)

question: When does the first stage of labour officially come to an end?

options.A: When regular uterine contractions first begin
options.B: When the baby's head emerges from the vagina
options.C: When the placenta is successfully delivered
options.D: When the cervix is fully dilated at 10 centimeters

explanation: Stage one is all about opening the cervix. Once it hits 10 cm, that stage is wrapped up and it's time to push!

question: Why is it so important to report an accidental needle-stick or blood exposure immediately?

options.A: Post-exposure preventative treatments work best when started quickly
options.B: Agency managers need time to discipline the careless worker
options.C: Insurance companies will refuse claims filed after twenty-four hours
options.D: State laws make late reporting a criminal offense for nurses

explanation: Time matters! Preventive medicines for bloodborne infections like HIV or Hepatitis B work best when taken very soon after an exposure.

question: Why does a skin pinch test help nurses check a patient's hydration level?

options.A: Electrolyte imbalances cause immediate muscle contractions under the skin
options.B: Lack of blood flow makes the skin permanently thick and rigid
options.C: Dehydrated skin loses elasticity because interstitial fluid is depleted
options.D: Fever causes the skin cells to lock together tightly

explanation: When the fluid between skin cells dries up, the skin loses its natural stretchiness and takes longer to bounce back flat after pinching.

question: Why do we use an interdisciplinary team in palliative care?

options.A: It reduces the total number of staff members needed in a hospital
options.B: It covers the diverse physical, emotional, and spiritual needs of the patient
options.C: It prevents families from speaking with the healthcare team
options.D: It ensures that doctors make all decisions without consulting others

explanation: Fantastic! Because end-of-life care touches every part of a person's life, it takes a diverse team of experts to cover all their physical, emotional, and spiritual needs.

question: Why might a patient on a ventilator for a long time be switched from an ordinary breathing tube (endotracheal tube) to a tracheostomy?

options.A: To completely eliminate the risk of respiratory infections
options.B: To reduce damage to the vocal cords and larynx
options.C: To allow the patient to swallow solid food immediately
options.D: To make the ventilator machine run faster

explanation: Endotracheal tubes passing through the mouth can hurt the vocal cords over time. Moving to a tracheostomy protects the larynx during long-term care.

question: How does community-based care differ from hospital care regarding patient freedom?

options.A: There is no difference in personal autonomy between the two settings
options.B: Institutional care gives patients more freedom to choose their meal times
options.C: Community care relies strictly on hospital staff to dictate daily actions
options.D: Community care allows clients greater autonomy over their daily routines

explanation: Brilliant! At home, clients keep their freedom and call the shots on their everyday daily routines.

question: Why would a patient who took a severe drug overdose be put on a mechanical ventilator?

options.A: Reversal of central nervous system toxicity
options.B: Immediate elimination of the drug from the lungs
options.C: Airway protection and respiratory support
options.D: Prevention of future drug dependency

explanation: When someone is deeply unconscious from an overdose, their body forgets to protect its own airway. The ventilator keeps them breathing safely and stops any spit or vomit from entering their lungs.

question: Which of the following is considered the most effective way to prevent the spread of infections?

options.A: Using private rooms
options.B: Proper hand hygiene
options.C: Wearing sterile gowns
options.D: Taking daily vitamins

explanation: Washing hands or using alcohol rubs removes transient microorganisms from the skin, stopping cross-contamination. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h4)

question: Why are clinical supervision and peer support so important for nurses working in crisis settings?

options.A: They ensure that nurses never feel empathy for their patients
options.B: They are used primarily to penalize nurses who make charting errors
options.C: They help prevent burnout and address secondary trauma from exposure to crisis stories
options.D: They replace the need for formal psychiatric nursing education

explanation: You cannot pour from an empty cup! Supervision and peer debriefing give you a safe space to offload emotional stress and protect your own mental health.

question: Why is teaching children not to share personal items so important in schools?

options.A: Teachers are legally required to diagnose skin conditions during morning assembly
options.B: Children frequently exchange items like combs and caps, spreading fungal and parasitic infections
options.C: Sharing clothes is the only known method of bacterial transmission
options.D: Schools lack the budget to buy chemical disinfectants for classroom desks

explanation: Kids love sharing caps and combs, which unfortunately makes it super easy to pass around things like lice and ringworm!

question: Why is it necessary to use redundant communication systems during a disaster response?

options.A: Radio frequencies are too expensive for humanitarian groups
options.B: Paper notes are too heavy to carry around a disaster zone
options.C: Different agencies are legally banned from using mobile phones
options.D: Standard cellular networks and internet lines frequently collapse

explanation: Disasters routinely destroy power grids and cell towers, so teams need backup tools like satellite radios and runners. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h5)

question: What is a major risk if a patient stops taking their antibiotics early because they start feeling better?

options.A: The body will stop making white blood cells
options.B: The infection can return stronger and cause long-term damage
options.C: The ovaries will immediately double in size
options.D: The patient will instantly develop kidney failure

explanation: Always educate your patients to finish their drugs! Stopping early leaves the toughest bacteria alive to bounce back harder and cause scarring.

question: You check a toddler's growth chart and notice their weight curve has suddenly crossed downward across two major percentile lines. What should you suspect?

options.A: Normal adolescent growth spurt
options.B: Accurate measurement error by the clinic staff
options.C: Excessive physical activity and exercise
options.D: Possible nutritional deficiency or illness

explanation: Spot on! A downward drop across major percentile lines is a classic red flag for growth faltering. It's our cue to investigate for hidden illness or poor feeding.

question: How does dietetics mainly differ from general nutrition study?

options.A: Analyzing the chemical structure of carbohydrates
options.B: Studying how plants absorb nutrients from soil
options.C: Translating nutrition science into practical dietary plans
options.D: Manufacturing vitamin supplements for hospitals

explanation: You've got this! While nutrition looks at the science of food, dietetics takes those facts and turns them into real, everyday meal plans that help people get well or stay healthy.

question: What is the main goal of using a qualitative approach in a nursing study?

options.A: To find the exact percentage of patients cured by a drug
options.B: To measure the physical strength recovery of post-op clients
options.C: To gain a deep understanding of lived human experiences
options.D: To prove a mathematical relationship between two variables

explanation: Qualitative research helps us walk in our patients' shoes and truly understand what they are going through emotionally.

question: What is the primary goal of social services for persons with physical disabilities?

options.A: Eliminating all physical impairments completely
options.B: Providing permanent institutional care for everyone
options.C: Promoting independence and equal participation
options.D: Replacing the need for medical rehabilitation

explanation: Social services focus on empowering individuals to live as independently as possible and take part in society on an equal basis with others. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T16#GNS225_U5_T16_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of a clinical audit in a hospital?

options.A: Comparing current nursing practice against established standards
options.B: Counting the number of visitors on a ward
options.C: Calculating the monthly salary of nursing staff
options.D: Checking the expiration dates of food in the canteen

explanation: A clinical audit is simply checking our actual bedside practice against the golden standard of care to see how well we are doing.

question: What kind of work environment destroys long-term quality improvement?

options.A: A workplace with too many staff meetings
options.B: An environment that uses electronic medical records
options.C: A hospital that provides regular free training
options.D: A toxic or purely punitive work environment

explanation: Fear of punishment stops staff from reporting errors or speaking up about why a new protocol is failing. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why does the pancreas secrete large amounts of bicarbonate into the small intestine?

options.A: To neutralize the acidic chyme coming from the stomach
options.B: To break down complex fat molecules directly
options.C: To turn liquid chyme into a solid fecal mass
options.D: To activate salivary amylase in the upper intestine

explanation: Bicarbonate is alkaline, meaning it cools down the harsh acid coming from the stomach, protecting your intestines and creating the right environment for enzymes to work. Well done!

question: Why must school management regularly inspect food vendors working on school grounds?

options.A: To determine which meals are most popular among the teachers
options.B: To replace the school kitchen staff with professional chefs
options.C: To collect daily taxes from food sellers for the school account
options.D: To prevent foodborne illnesses and ensure high hygiene standards

explanation: Spot on! Routine checks protect everyone on campus from contaminated meals and poor food handling habits.

question: Which of the following is an example of a proactive risk mitigation strategy?

options.A: Filing an incident report after a wrong drug was given
options.B: Apologizing to a family after a surgical complication
options.C: Checking emergency crash carts at the start of every shift
options.D: Investigating why a patient fell out of bed last night

explanation: Checking equipment before an emergency happens is proactive because it stops failure before a patient is harmed. [learn more](GST319_U4_T6#GST319_U4_T6_h4)

question: How do local disaster teams handle poor or flooded roads during an emergency?

options.A: By waiting months until the floodwaters dry up completely
options.B: By demanding that heavy trucks drive through flooded bridges anyway
options.C: by halting all relief distribution until federal contractors fix the roads
options.D: By utilizing alternative transport methods like local boats, canoes, and motorcycles

explanation: Well done! When big trucks can't pass, using local boats, canoes, or bikes is a smart way to get supplies to people who are cut off.

question: A nurse is trying to calculate a drug dose, but the screen is cluttered with pop-ups, flashing icons, and tiny text. What is this poor design causing?

options.A: Decreased physical fatigue
options.B: Excessive cognitive load
options.C: Enhanced user satisfaction
options.D: Improved clinical efficiency

explanation: You got it! Cluttered screens force your brain to waste energy sorting through useless distractions, overloading your mental capacity.

question: When doing a quick ABCDE emergency check on a patient, what does the letter 'C' stand for?

options.A: Coughing
options.B: Circulation
options.C: Consciousness
options.D: Cyanosis

explanation: A is Airway, B is Breathing, and C is Circulation! You check pulses and bleeding here. Easy peasy!

question: A patient has acute Hepatitis B. Which part of their history helps you trace how they caught it?

options.A: Swimming in a public pool with high chlorine levels
options.B: Eating unwashed raw vegetables from a local market stall
options.C: Receiving an unscreened blood transfusion or sharing needles
options.D: Drinking untreated well water during a rural community visit

explanation: Spot on! Hepatitis B is a bloodborne infection, meaning it spreads through contact with infected blood or sharp objects like needles and unsterilized blades.

question: What is the main benefit of using predictive equations in clinical settings?

options.A: They eliminate the need to know the patient's weight
options.B: They provide the absolute most accurate measurement possible
options.C: They are quick and easy to calculate without special equipment
options.D: They directly measure the heat released from human skin

explanation: Spot on! When you don't have expensive laboratory gadgets in the ward, predictive equations let nurses quickly estimate a patient's calorie needs using basic measurements.

question: What is the main purpose of an Electronic Health Record (EHR)?

options.A: To prevent patients from viewing their own medical test results
options.B: To store hospital financial budgets and staff work schedules
options.C: To replace traditional bedside nursing care with automated machines
options.D: To provide digital patient charts that can be shared across care settings

explanation: Spot on! EHRs put patient info into digital charts so healthcare teams can share accurate details safely across different departments. You've got this!

question: Why is accurate nutritional documentation important among members of the healthcare team?

options.A: It replaces the need for verbal shift handovers entirely
options.B: It prevents the hospital from having to buy specialized nutritional supplements
options.C: It ensures clear communication between nurses, doctors, and dietitians for coordinated care
options.D: It is only used for insurance billing and has no role in clinical treatment

explanation: Clear notes allow every healthcare provider involved in the patient's care to understand their nutritional status and treatment plan. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h7)

question: A patient refuses to leave their house because they are terrified of having a panic attack in public and not being able to escape. What is this called?

options.A: Generalized anxiety disorder
options.B: Obsessive-compulsive disorder
options.C: Agoraphobia
options.D: Social anxiety disorder

explanation: You nailed it. Agoraphobia is the fear of being trapped in public spaces where escape feels hard, which often leads people to stay safely inside their homes.

question: Which of these is a common risk for patients during a long-distance medical transport?

options.A: Permanent loss of hearing from quiet cabin environments
options.B: Rapid weight gain due to intravenous fluid retention
options.C: Sudden complete recovery from chronic illnesses
options.D: Hypothermia and pressure sores from rigid stretchers

explanation: Lying still on a hard stretcher in a cold vehicle for hours puts the patient at high risk for skin breakdown and dropping body temperature.

question: In midwifery, what does the term 'foetal attitude' actually mean?

options.A: The rate of cervical dilation over a specific time period
options.B: The position of the placenta inside the lower uterine segment
options.C: The relationship of foetal body parts to one another
options.D: The emotional mood of the mother during contractions

explanation: Don't let the word 'attitude' confuse you—it simply describes how the baby's head and limbs are curled up against its trunk (usually tucked in nicely like a little ball).

question: Why must pregnant women avoid eating raw or undercooked meats?

options.A: Raw meat causes severe allergic skin rashes in expectant mothers
options.B: Because cooked meat has more protein than raw meat
options.C: To prevent dangerous foodborne infections that can harm the pregnancy
options.D: Undercooked meat takes much longer for the stomach to digest

explanation: Raw meat can hide tricky germs and parasites like toxoplasma. Cooking food thoroughly keeps both mum and baby safe from infections!

question: What is the main goal of Directly Observed Therapy (DOT) for TB patients?

options.A: Reducing the overall financial cost of purchasing prescription drugs
options.B: Eliminating the need for periodic sputum laboratory testing
options.C: Ensuring patients swallow every medication dose to prevent resistance
options.D: Allowing nurses to monitor daily lung function and oxygen saturation

explanation: With DOT, a health worker watches the patient take their drugs. This stops missed doses and prevents drug-resistant TB strains from forming.

question: What happens when a researcher makes a Type I error?

options.A: Concluding a treatment works when it actually does not
options.B: Failing to notice that a treatment works when it actually does
options.C: Selecting a sample that is too small to represent the ward
options.D: Calculating the wrong average for patient blood pressures

explanation: Correct! A Type I error is like celebrating a false positive—thinking your new nursing routine helps patients when it really doesn't do anything special.

question: At a hot outdoor concert, a nurse notices attendees feeling dizzy, nauseous, and sweating heavily. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Immediately discharge them from the venue without further assessment
options.B: Administer powerful intravenous antibiotics to all affected individuals
options.C: Move them to a shaded cooling area and provide oral rehydration
options.D: Advise them to continue dancing until the concert concludes

explanation: Classic signs of heat exhaustion! Getting them out of the sun and giving fluids right away stops it from turning into heatstroke.

question: Why must a healthcare plan include flexibility?

options.A: To allow staff to come to work whenever they feel like it.
options.B: To prevent the government from auditing the facility.
options.C: To handle unexpected clinical crises and emergencies smoothly.
options.D: To make it easier to change the hospital name and logo.

explanation: Medical environments change rapidly due to emergencies, requiring plans that can bend without breaking.

question: Which screening test uses a low-dose X-ray to spot tiny lumps and microcalcifications before anyone can even feel them?

options.A: Clinical inspection
options.B: Breast self-examination
options.C: Mammography
options.D: Ultrasound scanning

explanation: Mammography is fantastic for early catch because it spots microscopic changes long before your fingers ever could.

question: What is a great quality to look for when picking members for a QI team?

options.A: Preference for keeping current hospital routines unchanged
options.B: High seniority status and administrative authority only
options.C: Curiosity about how things work and respect from peers
options.D: Experience working exclusively on the night shift

explanation: Spot on! Good team members need open minds to question old routines and enough respect from coworkers to get others on board.

question: How do research objectives connect to your main research question?

options.A: Objectives replace the research question entirely during data analysis
options.B: Objectives are guesses made before looking at the research question
options.C: Objectives explain why the research question is impossible to answer
options.D: Objectives break the main question down into smaller, actionable steps

explanation: Think of objectives as the stepping stones. They take your big main research question and slice it into smaller, bite-sized goals you can achieve one by one.

question: What is the primary physiological mechanism that causes pressure injuries to form over bony prominences?

options.A: Excessive surface sweat softens the outer skin layer until it tears
options.B: Prolonged pressure cuts off capillary blood flow, causing tissue ischemia
options.C: Bacterial growth multiplies rapidly inside healthy sweat glands
options.D: The body's immune system attacks normal skin cells by mistake

explanation: When external pressure exceeds normal capillary pressure, blood flow stops, starving the tissues of oxygen and nutrients and causing cell death. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h7)

question: What is the best way to communicate with a patient who has a hearing impairment?
